summary: Capcom's supernatural samurai action series; modern PC remasters win where they exist, but the Xbox Genma version, original PS2 bonus media, mobile/live-service entries, and future releases need explicit caveats.

entries.title: Onimusha: Warlords
entries.definitive_edition: PC HD remaster plus Genma Onimusha secondary content

emulation.emulator: None for PC remaster; xemu for Genma Onimusha
emulation.notes: Use xemu/original Xbox for Genma-exclusive content.

primary.why: The PC HD remaster has the highest fidelity and modern controls, with widescreen support, smoother framerate, rerecorded soundtrack, and easier weapon switching.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam PC remaster; then sample Genma Onimusha on Xbox or Xbox emulation for its exclusive tower/armor/green-soul content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Genma Onimusha adds better graphics, new gameplay additions, 5.1 audio, extra armors, a new tower area, and green-soul mechanics absent from the HD remaster.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Xbox Genma-exclusive tower and bonus systems after the remaster if you want every version-specific addition.
secondary.why: The HD remaster is higher fidelity overall but explicitly does not include Genma Onimusha features.

all_releases.reason: skip: historically central, but superseded for fidelity by the HD remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: Genma Onimusha expanded Xbox version with extra gameplay, armor, tower area, and 5.1 audio.
all_releases.reason: secondary: exclusive content absent from the HD remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: Original limited Windows port available in China and Russia.
all_releases.reason: skip: superseded by the worldwide HD remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: HD remaster with widescreen, modern controls, smoother framerate, and rerecorded soundtrack.
all_releases.reason: skip: same remaster family, but PC has the highest fidelity ceiling.
primary: highest-fidelity main playthrough for Warlords.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The PC HD remaster is the fidelity pick, but it does not include Genma Onimusha's Xbox-exclusive tower, armor, and green-soul additions.

entries.remaster_caveats: HD remaster omits Genma Onimusha features and rerecords the soundtrack.

entries.title: Onimusha 2: Samurai's Destiny
entries.definitive_edition: PC HD remaster plus PS2 bonus-media check

emulation.emulator: None for PC remaster; PCSX2 for PS2 bonus media
emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 or original PS2 to check removed bonus media.

primary.why: The PC remaster runs at high resolution/60fps, supports widescreen, adds modern analog controls and quality-of-life changes, and unlocks bonus materials from the start.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam PC remaster; use the original PS2 release only to view the removed original bonus videos/idle music video/Onimusha 3 teaser.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original special-option material removed from the remaster, including a making-of clip, an Onimusha 3 teaser, and the idle title-screen music video.
secondary.what_to_play: Boot the PS2 original's special/bonus menus to view the removed media after finishing the remaster.
secondary.why: The remaster is the main playthrough, but the PS2 original retains bonus media absent from the remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PS2 release with bonus media later removed from the remaster.
all_releases.reason: secondary: only for original bonus media not present in the remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: HD remaster with 60fps, widescreen, modern controls, quick weapon switching, Japanese dialogue option, and bonus materials unlocked from the start.
all_releases.reason: skip: same remaster family, but PC has the highest fidelity ceiling.
primary: highest-fidelity main playthrough.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The remaster is the fidelity and gameplay pick, but the PS2 original preserves several removed special-option media items.

entries.remaster_caveats: Remaster removes some original bonus video/media content while adding high-res/60fps, widescreen, controls, Japanese dialogue, and quality-of-life features.

primary.why: Onimusha Tactics is a GBA-only tactical RPG spin-off; high-quality GBA emulation gives the cleanest preservation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GBA release through mGBA with integer scaling and original aspect ratio, or on original GBA hardware.

all_releases.reason: primary: only documented platform route.

emulation.notes: Use original PS2 hardware if local multiplayer setup is preferred.

primary.why: Blade Warriors is a PS2-only platform-fighter spin-off; PCSX2 gives the best practical image quality while preserving the original game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on original PS2 hardware for local multiplayer.

all_releases.reason: primary: only documented platform route.

entries.title: Onimusha 3: Demon Siege

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution and widescreen only if stable/accurate.

primary.why: The Windows port is documented as a weak conversion with low framerate and sound issues, so the PS2 original via PCSX2 is the best fidelity/completeness balance.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution; avoid the old PC port unless researching its historical conversion.

all_releases.reason: primary: best version balance when upscaled through PCSX2.

all_releases.fidelity: PC port criticized for low framerate, missing/poor sound effects, and feeling like a quick PS2 conversion.
all_releases.reason: skip: worse conversion quality than the PS2 original via emulation.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Native PC would normally win on fidelity, but the documented quality problems make upscaled PS2 the recommended route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No HD remaster documented as of this entry.

primary.why: Curtain of Darkness is a Japan-only mobile Onimusha release with no modern port documented.
primary.how_to_play: Treat as an archival mobile title; no current official modern route is documented.

all_releases.reason: primary: only documented platform route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Released mobile title, but current availability/preservation route is unclear.

primary.why: Dawn of Dreams is a PS2-only main-series sequel with no modern port documented; PCSX2 provides the highest practical fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on original PS2 hardware.

all_releases.reason: primary: only documented platform route.

entries.title: Onimusha Essentials
entries.definitive_edition: PS2 compilation for collection purposes only

emulation.notes: Use individual modern remasters where available.

primary.why: Onimusha Essentials bundles Warlords, Onimusha 2, and Onimusha 3 for PS2; it is useful as a historical compilation, but not the best route for Warlords or Onimusha 2 after their remasters.
primary.how_to_play: Use only as a PS2 collection convenience; follow the individual game entries for the best-version recommendations.

all_releases.fidelity: Compilation of the first three PS2-era Onimusha titles.
all_releases.reason: primary: only documented compilation route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Convenient PS2 package, but the first two games now have higher-fidelity remasters.

entries.title: Onimusha Soul

primary.why: Onimusha Soul began as a browser-based game before mobile and PS3 releases; as a shut-down service, it is an archival entry rather than a currently playable recommendation.
primary.how_to_play: No current official route is documented; treat as a defunct online/service game unless preserved materials are available.

all_releases.reason: primary: base release of the service, now archival.
skip: service shut down; no current official route.
skip: service/live-game availability is defunct or not documented as currently playable.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Online-service game with no current official playable route documented.

primary.how_to_play: Play at a participating Japanese arcade/location if available; no home port is documented.
